primaryChecks.text: Now some of the Hebrews had gone over the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead; but as for Saul, he was yet in Gilgal, and all the people followed him trembling.
primaryChecks.previousContext: When the men of Israel saw that they were in trouble (for the people were distressed), then the people hid themselves in caves, in thickets, in rocks, in tombs, and in pits.
primaryChecks.nextContext: He stayed seven days, according to the time set by Samuel; but Samuel didn’t come to Gilgal, and the people were scattering from him.

primaryChecks.text: When the men of Israel who were on the other side of the valley, and those who were beyond the Jordan, saw that the men of Israel fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned the cities and fled; and the Philistines came and lived in them.
primaryChecks.previousContext: So Saul died with his three sons, his armor bearer, and all his men that same day together.
primaryChecks.nextContext: On the next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
